[03 — Art runtimes](03-art-runtimes.md) is about which runtime you pick as a creator. This page is
about what a runtime **is**: what it gets handed, what it is forbidden to do, and what that rules
out of your art before you draw a line of it.

Read it if you are designing art whose behaviour depends on anything, and read the last two
sections before you write a bespoke runtime — someone already wrote one against a mental model this
page would have corrected, and found out at the wrong end of the process.

## The short version

- A render is a **pure function of three things**: the token's immutable identity, your own
  configuration bytes, and your pool's market state. Nothing else is reachable.
- **A runtime cannot read state from other contracts.** Not your staking contract, not a holder
  count, not an activation tier. `renderV1` makes no external call at all.
- **Almost nobody needs their own runtime.** The launchable path is a shared generic runtime you
  configure with parameters. You deploy nothing and register nothing.
- A bespoke runtime is an **operator** action through the protocol Safe, not something a creator
  ships. And **registering one proves almost nothing** — see [the registration
  gate](#the-registration-gate-proves-three-things-and-your-art-is-none-of-them).

## What a runtime is handed, and nothing else

One call, one calldata struct. `ArtRequestV1`:

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | `uint256` | Your project's id in the registry |
| `tokenId` | `uint256` | Which token is being rendered |
| `dna` | `bytes32` | This token's identity. Fixed forever at mint |
| `bornBlock` | `uint64` | The block the token was minted in |
| `awakenCount` | `uint32` | How many times this token has been awakened |
| `artConfig` | `bytes` | **Your own configuration bytes**, reconstructed from the project's immutable script pointers |
| `state` | `ArtStateV1` | The bounded market snapshot below |

The struct's own note is worth quoting, because it is the design and not a summary of it: *no
caller address, no block, no timestamp, no randomness*. Those are absent so that a render is
replayable by anyone, at any time, from chain state alone.

### `ArtStateV1` — the 22 market fields

This is the **entire** market surface. There is no second reader, no escape hatch, and no raw pool
access.

| Field | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normalizedTick` | `int24` | Last observed tick, **normalized so higher always means the project token appreciated** |
| `athNormalizedTick` | `int24` | Monotone maximum `normalizedTick` ever observed |
| `drawdownTicks` | `uint32` | `ath - current`, in normalized ticks. `0` at a new high, never negative |
| `maxDrawdownTicks` | `uint32` | Monotone maximum drawdown ever observed |
| `recoveryTicks` | `uint32` | `maxDrawdown - currentDrawdown`: how far price has climbed back |
| `volatilityTickMovement` | `uint64` | Cumulative `abs(delta normalizedTick)` — price **path length**, movement-weighted |
| `volumeTier` | `uint32` | Doubling ladder over cumulative organic quote volume. Split-invariant |
| `epoch` | `uint32` | One epoch per 16x of cumulative organic quote volume. Monotone |
| `stressTier` | `uint32` | Derived, bounded ladder over `drawdownTicks` |
| `organicBuyVolume` | `uint256` | Cumulative organic BUY volume, quote-asset wei |
| `organicSellVolume` | `uint256` | Cumulative organic SELL volume, quote-asset wei |
| `organicQuoteVolume` | `uint256` | Their sum, quote-asset wei |
| `organicProjectVolume` | `uint128` | Cumulative organic project-token volume, project-token wei |
| `netQuoteFlow` | `int256` | Signed net quote flow, buys positive, quote-asset wei |
| `trackedLiquidityUnits` | `uint128` | Sum of authorized liquidity deltas, **in units of Uniswap L** |
| `observedActiveLiquidity` | `uint128` | PoolManager's actual active liquidity at the last observed tick, units of Uniswap L |
| `observationSequence` | `uint64` | Monotone index over all observations |
| `fragmentation` | `uint32` | The organic swap **count**, saturated — a temporal metric, not an economic one |
| `quoteDecimals` | `uint8` | The quote asset's decimals, so you can render volumes honestly |
| `historyCommitment` | `bytes32` | Chained commitment over the whole observation stream |
| `schemaVersion` | `uint8` | This struct's version, so a runtime can refuse a shape it does not understand |
| `complete` | `bool` | True only when every field above was read from the hook |

Three properties this struct exists to enforce, so that no renderer has to remember them:

1. **Direction is already decided.** Every tick is normalized: higher always means the project token
   appreciated against its quote, in both currency orderings. The raw, order-dependent tick is
   deliberately absent and must never be added.
2. **Magnitude drives major state.** Every field you may use to advance a major visual state comes
   from economic magnitude — quote volume, price movement — never from the number of observations.
   `fragmentation` is the honest count of swaps, kept under a name that says what it is, and the
   configuration format refuses it as a visual-layer driver.
3. **No mislabelled liquidity, no quote-asset assumption.** `trackedLiquidityUnits` and
   `observedActiveLiquidity` are both units of Uniswap L. Neither is a token amount, neither is
   WETH-specific, and they are never interchanged.

`complete == false` means the snapshot is partial. A renderer is never asked to guess: the launch
already proved the hook answers every field, so the collection reports the impossible state instead
of rendering it as if everything were zero.

## The rule that decides what art is possible

> **`renderV1` and `tokenUriV1` MUST be `view` and MUST make no external call.**

That is the interface's own requirement, not a convention. The collection-side identity a runtime
needs to build a complete `tokenURI` — collection name and symbol, the runtime id, the config,
trait-schema and market-mapping hashes, the project-page base — is passed **in**, as a separate
`TokenIdentityV1` struct, for a stated reason: so the runtime *"cannot reach into the collection, and
a caller cannot induce it to reach anywhere else."* The request carries no address a runtime could be
talked into calling.

**So a runtime cannot read project-specific state from other contracts.** In plain words, and this
is the part to internalise before you design:

- No staking balances, no lock durations, no "staked for 30 days" tier.
- No activation, subscription, tier or level tracked anywhere but the token itself.
- No holder counts, no leaderboard position, no rank against other holders.
- No per-token records the collection does not itself hold.
- No oracle, no price feed other than your own pool's recorded state, no cross-chain read.
- No allowlist, no off-chain signature, no "unlocked by owning X".

Your art reacts to **the market** and to **the token's own identity**. That is the whole input set.
If your concept is "the piece evolves when the holder stakes it", the runtime cannot see that, and
no amount of contract work on your side will make it visible — the call that would read it is the
call the interface forbids.

What you *can* react to per token: `dna` (immutable), `bornBlock`, `awakenCount`, and your own
`artConfig`. `awakenCount` is the only per-token value that moves, and it moves through the
collection, not through a contract of yours.

The trade is deliberate. Purity is what makes the render replayable by anyone from chain state
alone, forever, with no server and no trust in you — which is the property the collection is sold
on. A runtime that could call out would be a runtime whose output depends on what some other
contract said at read time, and an owner of that contract could change the art.

## Almost nobody needs their own runtime

The launchable path does not involve writing or deploying a contract at all.

`LAUNCHABLE_ART_RUNTIMES` is **`["SOLIDITY_SVG"]`** today. That is one shared, vetted singleton per
chain — `SolidityGenerativeRuntimeV1` — used by every `SOLIDITY_SVG_V1` project on that chain. You
supply **ACV1 parameters** in your bundle and the launch binds them to that runtime:

- a palette (up to 8 RGB entries) and a background slot;
- up to 8 **layers**, each one a drawing primitive (`STRATA`, `RINGS`, `BARS`, `GRID`, `SHARDS`,
  `VEIL`), the market sensor that drives its magnitude, a response curve (`LINEAR`, `LOG2`, `EASE`,
  `STEP`), a palette slot, and the element-count band it maps into;
- up to 8 **traits**, each a name, a source (a sensor or a DNA slot) and a style (`NUMBER`, `WORD`,
  `HEX`);
- an optional title, and an `ANIMATE` flag.

Two projects on this runtime differ because their configurations differ. That is the point of the
design: the runtime it replaced took a config and ignored it, so every project it rendered would
have looked the same.

**The other approved runtimes are preview-only.** `ONCHAIN_JAVASCRIPT_V1` is approved by the bundle
format — templates on it scaffold, preview, validate and export — and no launch binds it. The
protocol refuses it in three independent places: `ArtRuntimeRegistryV1.modeAvailable` is `pure` and
answers true for `SOLIDITY_SVG_V1` alone, so a JavaScript runtime cannot even be **registered**;
`ProjectCollectionV1.bindArt` reverts `ArtModeNotAvailable` for any other mode; and the factory
refuses it a third time when its art lane is wired at initialization, so a misconfigured lane fails
then rather than at the first creator's launch. `STATIC_IMAGE_V1` is refused because no static
project type exists in the `.relics` schema for it to serve.

> **Two enums in this system give the value `1` opposite meanings, and one of them is what your
> `runtimeMode()` returns.** `ArtRuntimeMode` — the one an `IArtRuntimeV1` implementation reports —
> is `NONE = 0`, `SOLIDITY_SVG_V1 = 1`, `ONCHAIN_JAVASCRIPT_V1 = 2`, `STATIC_IMAGE_V1 = 3`. The
> launch-parameter enum the creator kit mirrors, `ILaunchpad.ArtMode`, is `SOLIDITY_SVG = 0`,
> `JAVASCRIPT = 1`. Return the named `ArtRuntimeMode` constant, never a bare literal: a `1` written
> against the wrong enum states the exact inverse of the intent, in the one place that binds a
> project's art lane permanently.

The registry's stated reason for gating JavaScript: that mode needs a content-addressed generator
plus its dependencies, an `animation_url` that reconstructs the real project, the **same** runtime
executing in the studio sandbox, and an `image` that is a deterministic representative render from
that same code, config, seed and state. This release proves none of that leg, so the mode is refused
rather than shipped half-built. Mode availability is `pure` on purpose — it cannot be switched on by
an authority key, a governance vote or a mistake. It takes a new implementation, published and then
installed, which is a visible and reviewable act rather than a parameter write.

## A bespoke runtime is an operator action, not a creator one

If you still need one, understand who performs each step. The request process itself — what to
build, how to open the pull request, what gets reviewed and what happens after approval — is
[Requesting a custom art runtime](../creator-kit/requesting-an-art-runtime.md).

**You implement all seven methods of `IArtRuntimeV1`:**

| Method | Mutability | What it must do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `renderV1(ArtRequestV1)` | `view` | Render one artwork. Must not revert for any configuration your own `validateConfigV1` accepted, and must make no external call |
| `tokenUriV1(ArtRequestV1, TokenIdentityV1)` | `view` | Render **and** assemble the complete `tokenURI` document. Same constraints |
| `validateConfigV1(bytes)` | `view` | Exhaustive configuration validation, run inside the atomic launch. `0` means valid. Returns the trait-schema commitment alongside the verdict |
| `runtimeTag()` | `pure` | A stable family identity, e.g. `keccak256("SOLIDITY_SVG_V1")` |
| `runtimeMode()` | `pure` | The `ArtRuntimeMode` value you implement |
| `runtimeVersion()` | `pure` | Monotonic version within the family |
| `maxOutputBytes()` | `pure` | Worst-case byte length `renderV1` can return, so an integrator can size a read without discovering the bound at runtime |

Document assembly lives in the runtime rather than the collection for two reasons that point the
same way: the metadata format is part of what a runtime version *means*, so it should be vetted and
pinned with the rest of it; and `ProjectCollection` is bounded by EIP-170 while the runtime
singleton has room.

**Someone else registers it.** `registerRuntime(uint32 runtimeId, address runtime, string label)` is
`onlyUpgradeAuthority` — the protocol 2-of-3 Safe. There is no permissionless registration path, and
no creator-supplied callee anywhere: a project's runtime is never an address a bundle names.

**Registration governs future launches only.** A project pins its runtime by **address and
codehash** into its own immutable binding at launch and reads them from there forever. `tokenURI`
never consults the registry. Deactivating a runtime stops the next launch; it cannot change one
artwork that already exists.

The security envelope around the call is structural rather than procedural: the target is an address
the project pinned at launch together with its codehash, the call is a `staticcall` so no state can
change and no reentrancy is possible, there is no `delegatecall` anywhere on the path, and the live
codehash is re-checked on every read — a metamorphic swap surfaces as a labelled renderer error
rather than silently rendering different art.

## The registration gate proves three things, and your art is none of them

**This is the trap.** Read it before you deploy anything.

`registerRuntime` identifies the contract by calling exactly three methods, each in `try`/`catch`:

```
runtimeMode()      →  must answer, and the mode must be one this release proved
runtimeVersion()   →  must answer
runtimeTag()       →  must answer
```

An address that fails any of them is refused with `RuntimeInterfaceMismatch`. Metadata is read *from*
the runtime rather than accepted from the caller, so a registry entry cannot describe a runtime as
something it is not.

That is the whole check. **Registration does not exercise `renderV1`, does not exercise
`tokenUriV1`, does not exercise `validateConfigV1`, does not read `maxOutputBytes`, and cannot check
the no-external-call rule at all.**

So: **a runtime implementing only those three `pure` methods registers successfully, and then fails
at the first render.** Nothing between registration and that first `tokenURI` call will tell you.

Where each failure actually lands:

| What is wrong | Where it surfaces | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing/reverting `runtimeMode`, `runtimeVersion`, `runtimeTag` | `registerRuntime` | Refused, Safe transaction reverts |
| A mode this release did not prove | `registerRuntime` | Refused, `RuntimeModeNotAvailable` |
| `validateConfigV1` rejects, reverts, or is missing | **The launch transaction** | Whole launch reverts, `ArtConfigRejected` |
| `renderV1` / `tokenUriV1` reverts, runs out of gas, makes an external call, or returns nothing | **Every `tokenURI` read, forever** | A live collection that renders no art |

The last row is not recoverable. The binding is one-shot and has no setter; a launched project's
runtime address and codehash cannot be changed by anyone, including the Safe. The collection catches
the revert and returns a `RENDERER_ERROR` document — it names the project, names the failure code,
and **deliberately shows no image**, because no branch substitutes generic, sample, placeholder or
another project's art. Silence is honest; a stand-in image is not. That behaviour is correct and it
is not a rescue.

**Successful registration is not validation. Test the render paths on a fork first**, against real
launched state, for the configurations you intend to allow — including the boundary ones your
`validateConfigV1` accepts but you never drew by hand. Confirm `renderV1` and `tokenUriV1` are
non-reverting **by construction** rather than by luck: bound every loop by a validated count,
preallocate every buffer to a capacity the validated element budget cannot exceed, and make every
arithmetic operation either bounded by a validated field or saturating. The shipped runtime is
written that way on purpose, and its own note says why — there is nothing on its path that could
revert on its behalf, because it makes no external call of any kind.

## What the collection checks around you

Worth knowing, because it tells you which failures are yours and which are already handled. At
`tokenURI` time, in order:

1. A runtime is bound at all, or `RENDER_ERR_UNBOUND`.
2. The runtime's live codehash equals the pinned one, or `RENDER_ERR_RUNTIME_CODE`.
3. The stored config chunks reconstruct to exactly the committed hash, or `RENDER_ERR_SCRIPT`.
4. The hook answers the whole art-state schema, or `RENDER_ERR_HOOK_STATE`.
5. Your `tokenUriV1` is called. A revert is `RENDER_ERR_RUNTIME_CALL`.
6. The result is checked: `ok` is true, `configCommitment` equals the collection's committed hash,
   the image-path and trait-path commitments agree, and the URI is non-empty — or
   `RENDER_ERR_CONFIG`.

Step 6 is why `ArtOutputV1` carries three separate commitments. `configCommitment` is
`keccak256(artConfig)` recomputed **inside** the render, so a caller can prove the bytes that were
rendered are the bytes it bound at launch. `visualTraitConfigHash` and `metadataTraitConfigHash` are
the same commitment computed on the image path and the trait path — equal by construction, because
one decode feeds one call — so a runtime whose picture and whose metadata drifted apart is caught
rather than served.

At launch, four things are proven rather than assumed, and any failure reverts the whole launch: the
pinned runtime holds the exact vetted code, the stored chunks reconstruct to the committed hash,
**the runtime itself accepts that configuration**, and the project's hook answers the whole art-state
schema. That ordering is what lets `tokenURI` be written with no fallback image: it is never handed
a configuration that cannot be drawn, because such a configuration cannot be launched.
